paragraphs: Here's what Psalm 50 is teaching, friend. God doesn't need a thing from us. He says every beast of the forest is His, the cattle on a thousand hills too, and He asks, "Do I eat the flesh of bulls, or drink the blood of goats?" (Psalm 50:10, 13). Your offerings were never a snack for God. He is not standing at the counter waiting for us to hand Him something, and that is GOOD news.

So what does He want? A thank offering, and vows kept (Psalm 50:14). Then He makes a promise: "Call upon Me in the day of trouble; I will deliver you, and you will honor Me." (Psalm 50:15). The heart of it is simple. Come to Him thankful, come to Him when it's hard, and trust that He is the one who rescues. Me, I got pulled out of a junk drawer, so I know a little about being rescued by Someone who didn't need me and wanted me anyway.

But the psalm has a warning, and I'm not gonna sneak past it. The wicked could recite God's statutes, but they hated His instruction and cast His words behind them (Psalm 50:16-17). God kept silent, and they thought He was just like them, until He said, "But now I rebuke you and accuse you to your face." (Psalm 50:21). Don't mistake God's patience for approval, baker. Hold onto the closing words: "He who sacrifices a thank offering honors Me, and to him who rightly orders his way, I will show the salvation of God." (Psalm 50:23). Say the words, then live them, and let thanks be the way you walk.
